subject: Marketplace co-sell packaging: regional SKU & playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Marketplace co-sell packaging: regional SKU & playbook

Morning team —

Quick kickoff on multi-cloud marketplace packaging. AWS, Azure, and GCP have different co-sell entry rules and regional reach; we need a one-pager playbook that maps:
- Which SKUs we publish per cloud (e.g., metered vs. subscription)
- Region coverage per SKU (US/EU/APAC priorities)
- Packaging differences required for co-sell eligibility (commit tiers, trial length)
- Hand-offs for partner sales motions (who owns partner-intro, who owns technical onboarding)

I attached a rough packaging-proposals.xlsx with an initial split (metered core generation, annual reserved on Dedicated, and a bring-your-own-license listing option). Please review with your POVs and call out any redlines by EOD Fri.

Primary questions:
1) For AWS: do we go metered + 1 annual reserved SKU in all regions, or limit reserved to US/EU initially?
2) For Azure: they push a plan-based listing for co-sell — do we mirror it across GCP or keep plan-only on Azure?
3) Identify any SKU names that will confuse customers (e.g., 'Dedicated Reserved' vs 'Dedicated Commitment')

I want a short decision matrix by Wednesday so we can sync with Maria (CloudChannel) and request marketplace onboarding slots.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace co-sell packaging: regional SKU & playbook

On 2026-02-20 09:12, Jonas Weber wrote:
> Morning team —
> 
> Quick kickoff on multi-cloud marketplace packaging...

Thanks, Jonas. I pushed a first pass into packaging-proposals.xlsx (tab: Vanessa_notes). High-level thoughts:
- AWS: Recommend metered + "Reserved Annual" SKU but only in US + EU for initial reserved rollout. APAC demand looks uneven and committed capacity will be hard to hit for Q2. Put a note: reserve SKU requires a minimum commit of $50k ARR for co-sell.
- Azure: Azure Marketplace requires plan-based SKUs for co-sell. If we want Azure co-sell, we need a plan (monthly/annual) with a marketplace-managed metering contract. That argues for plan-only on Azure initially.
- GCP: More favorable to both metered and subscription, but co-sell motion there is weaker. Suggest we publish metered across GCP regions first and evaluate subscription later.

I attached aws-region-cost-model.csv with backend cost estimates per region. If we publish reserved in EU, we must localize EMEA price bands.

Two asks:
1) Tessa — can you validate whether procurement paperwork differs materially for reserved SKUs?
2) Priyom — can you check channel co-sell criteria for Azure?

-V
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(attachment: packaging-proposals.xlsx; aws-region-cost-model.csv)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-21T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace co-sell packaging: regional SKU & playbook

Jonas / Vanessa —

Quick procurement check: reserved/annual SKUs change the purchase flow in two ways:
- PO vs. card billing: Reserved deals often require PO/contract; we must surface a SOW template and invoice cadence in the marketplace listing or in follow-up sales motions.
- Trial/usage windows: Some customers expect an on-platform trial before committing; for Reserved SKUs we should offer a 14-day sandbox but not a full metered trial.

For co-sell we also need a clear statement on data residency for EU listings — marketplace legal teams will flag default data redaction unless we include our EU deployment options. That will affect price bands on AWS EU listings.

Action items I propose:
A) Flag Reserved SKU regions: US/West, US-East, EU-West only for Q2.
B) Publish metered core in all listed regions for each cloud for Q2.
C) Add a 'BYO' (bring-your-own) license SKU for private deployments (Redwood Private) — this helps enterprise buyers who cannot run via marketplace.

I'll draft the procurement blurb and a short checklist for each SKU by Tuesday COB.

-Tessa
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
(attachment: procurement-sku-checklist.docx)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Maria Lopez <maria@cloudchannel.io>
Date: 2026-02-23T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace co-sell packaging: regional SKU & playbook

Looping Maria in from CloudChannel — Maria, welcome.

Summary of consensus so far:
- AWS: Metered across all supported regions; Reserved Annual SKU only in US + EU for initial launch (minimum commit $50k).
- Azure: Plan-based listings for co-sell; treat as plan-only for launch to meet their co-sell criteria.
- GCP: Metered first; evaluate subscription SKU in Q3 after initial telemetry.
- BYO Private SKU: Publish as a non-co-sell listing for enterprises that require VPC/on-prem.

Open items:
1) Exact SKU names and short descriptions (Jonas / Vanessa to finalize).
2) Pricing tiers per region (Vanessa to propose EU price bands).
3) Marketplace onboarding timeline (Maria: can CloudChannel get us earliest available slots?)

Proposed deadline: make final decisions by 2026-02-24 18:00 UTC so Jonas can send a consolidated playbook to partner teams.

-Priyom
Partner Programs Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Lopez <maria@cloudchannel.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace co-sell packaging: regional SKU & playbook

Thanks for the summary, Priyom — this looks good. A few clarifications from the partner ops side:
- Azure co-sell: plan-based listing is the right approach. We will need a partner-approved pricing sheet and a short 1-page technical compliance summary.
- AWS co-sell: reserved SKU in US + EU is a reasonable starting point. We'll aim to route co-sell opportunities via the AWS Partner Sales contact you included. Please note AWS requires a customer reference for reserved co-sell eligibility in some EMEA accounts.
- GCP: recommend starting metered in US/EU and limit APAC to regions where we can support SLA (Singapore, Tokyo).

I can secure marketplace onboarding slots for mid-March if you finalize the SKU names and the regional price grid this week. I also attached a DocuSign onboarding checklist — please sign the partner agreement at the link below after internal review.

DocuSign onboarding link: https://docusign.com/sign/abc-Redwood-Marketplace-Onboard
Shared playbook draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-marketplace-playbook

Happy to jump on a short sync if helpful.

Best —
Maria Lopez
Channel Partnerships, CloudChannel
(attachment: docusign-onboard-checklist.pdf)
